findings.passage: “Voting is a constitutional right.  Under the guise of preventing voter fraud, this bill would actually suppress the right to vote for many eligible voters in Pennsylvania who do not have a photo ID,” Hughes said.
findings.note: Release on the Senate passing House Bill 934, the photo-ID bill; he states his view of the bill on photo ID at the polls.

findings.passage: “The provisions of this bill almost amount to a poll tax, requiring mostly seniors to spend their valuable dollars to obtain a photo ID.”
findings.note: Same release; on the cost of obtaining an ID.

findings.passage: “This law is not about protecting against voter fraud, it is about the very real, systematic disenfranchisement of approximately 750,000 individuals – mostly the poor, the elderly, students and racial minorities. “It is voter suppression, plain and simple, and we must not stand for it.”
findings.note: Release on a Capitol rally against the 2012 voter ID law, where he also said he co-sponsored a bill to repeal it.

findings.passage: The bill attempts to enact unconstitutional voter ID requirements despite the thousands of people who don’t have what would be valid ID under the bill.  It also limits mail-in ballots and drop boxes, important choices for those who lack mobility or transportation.
findings.note: Text on his 'Defend the Vote' page about House Bill 1300 (voter ID and mail-ballot limits); page date taken from the page's publish metadata.
